declaration_timing: After the first optimizer updates, before any completed endpoint, export or score. The original fit recipe lacked an explicit practically useful effect threshold. This is a dated decision-policy addendum, not a claim of pre-fit registration.
rationale: The quality route asks for a nontrivial local WP change worth follow-up against a near-capacity control, with limited serving regression; the cost route asks for a material 20% latency reduction with only a small local score tradeoff. These are chosen allocation preferences, not estimated benefits, a universal threshold, a power calculation or a public-score conversion.
required_evidence: Full declared paired-cell analysis, all four exposed fold means and seed/component uncertainty, plus repeated same-machine CPU FP32 one-row stateful serving timing under identical threads/library/reset/input conditions. Report median and tail latency. No CPU win is established by the shared-GPU profiles.
uncertainty_policy: Point thresholds alone do not establish a robust win. Report interval scope, fold sensitivity and failures. An interval crossing zero is not a universal stop; inconclusive outcomes can justify a specifically bounded follow-up. A result below the thresholds is preserved and may be retained for a distinct blend/teacher or longer-schedule question, without relabeling this comparison positive.
convergence: Fixed six epochs remains the primary endpoint, not proof of convergence. Any longer schedule requires a distinct matched recipe declared before evaluation feedback is used to select its endpoint.
